Intensity-Duration-Frequency (IDF) curves are mathematical models used to describe the statistical behavior of intense precipitation at a point. IDF curves provide the average precipitation intensity as a function of duration and return period, and are the basis for the definition of They are the basis for the design of many engineering works, such as culverts, etc.

In Brazil, and in many other countries around the world, the average precipitation intensity $I$ over a certain period of time $t$ for a given return period $T$ is usually parameterized as follows,

$$I = \frac{aT^b}{(t+c)^d}$$
where $a$, $b$, $c$, and $d$ are parameters that must be estimated.

```{r}
a = 1574.7
b = 0.207
c = 11
d = 0.884
td = 1
i <- c(1:10:400)
F = 1 - (td + c)^(-d/b)*(a/i)^(1/b)
plot(F)
```
